EMPLOYEES' OLD-GE BENEFITS (PAYMENT OF INVALIDIY ALLOWANCE) REGULATIONS,
1981
EMPLOYEES' OLD-GE BENEFITS (PAYMENT OF INVALIDITY
ALLOWANCE) REGULATIONS, 1981
(Noti. S.R.O.448 (1) 32, dated May 11,
1982, Gaz, of Pak. Extr, Pt. II, May 17, 1982 p. 612--1982 PLS 49.)
1. Short title and commencement.‑(1) These regulations may be
called the Employees' Old‑Age Benefits (Payment of Invalidity Allowance)
Regulations, 1981.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. Definitions.‑(1) In these Regulations, unless there is
anything repugnant in the subject or context;
(a) "Act" means Employees'
Old‑Age Benefits Act, 1976 (XIV of 1976).
(b) "Allowance Book"
means a book issued to an Insured person under the regulations through which
Invalidity allowance shall be paid to the Insured person.
(c) "Claimant" means an
Insured Person who lodges a claim under these Regulations.
(d) "Form" means form
annexed to these Regulations.
(e) "Medical Board"
means a panel of doctors appointed by the Institution for assessing the degree
of Invalidity sustained by an Insured Person.
(f) "Permanent incapacity"
means an incapacity for at least a period of six months from the date of
sustaining invalidity.
(2) Words and expressions used in
these regulations‑but not defined herein shall have the same meaning as
are assigned to them in the Act.
3. An Insured Person who
sustains Invalidity shall notify the Insti tution the details of his Invalidity
on the prescribed claim form as soon as possible.
4. The Institution at any
stage may, in its discretion, call for further information from the claimant or
from his present or past employer which may be material In determining his
eligibility to resolve the Invalidity Allowance.
5. The Institution shall,
on scrutiny of the claim and on being satisfied that prima facie case exists
for payment of the Invalidity Allowance, refer the claimant to a medical board
for assessment of the degree of Invalidity.
6. Based on the findings
of the Medical Board, and the claimant otherwise being found entitled to
invalidity allowance, the Institution shall issue an allowance book containing
payment orders for such period as it may deem fit, but initially for a period
of not more than three months.
7. After expiry of three
months the Institution may refer the insured person to a Medical Board and on
the findings of Medical Board and the insured person otherwise being found
entitled to invalidity‑ allowance shall accordingly issue payment orders
for three months at a time during the period of invalidity.
8. The payment orders may
be encashed by the claimant from any Branch of a bank authorised by the
Institution for this purpose.
9. Where an Insured Person
is found in receipt of invalidity allowance to which he was not entitled, the
Institution may recover the amount so paid either by attachment of his wages or
by deduction from the allowance if any, payable under the Act or as arrears of
land revenue.
10. Notwithstanding
anything to the contrary contained in these regulations, the Institution may,
if it deems fit, after the period for which the payment orders will be issued
and medical examinations will he required. .
